questions.q: The points A(−1, −1), B(2, 3) and C(−2, 6) are the vertices of —
questions.work:
AB² = 3² + 4² = 25; BC² = 4² + 3² = 25; AC² = 1² + 7² = 50.
AB = BC and AB² + BC² = AC², so it is an isosceles right triangle.

questions.q: The point P with ordinate −3 divides the join of A(6, 5) and B(−1, 4) in the ratio —
questions.work:
Let the ratio be k : 1. y = (4k + 5)/(k + 1) = −3 ⇒ 4k + 5 = −3k − 3 ⇒ k = −8/7.
Negative k means external division in the ratio 8 : 7.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3) is ______. (b) Three points are collinear if the area of the triangle formed by them is ______.
questions.answer:
(a) ½ × base × height = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 square units.
(b) zero

questions.q: For A(1, 2), B(4, 6) and C(7, 2), find: (a) AB; (b) the midpoint of AC; (c) the centroid of ΔABC; (d) the area of ΔABC.
Find the ratio in which the line segment joining (2, −3) and (5, 6) is divided by the y-axis.
questions.answer:
Let the ratio be k : 1. On the y-axis x = 0: (5k + 2)/(k + 1) = 0 ⇒ k = −2/5.
So the y-axis divides it externally in the ratio 2 : 5.

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are (1, 2), (−2, 3) and (−3, −4).

questions.answer:
Area = ½|1(2 − 5) + 5(5 + 1) + 9(−1 − 2)| = ½|−3 + 30 − 27| = 0.
The area is zero, so the points are collinear.
